HON'BLE VINOD DIWAKAR, J. 
1.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. The instant petition has been preferred against the order dated 31.7.2025, passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-Ist, Lalitpur in Criminal Revision No.5 of 2025, titled Shailendra Chandel @ Harvendra Chandel & Ors v. State, whereby the order dated 20.12.2024, passed by the learned Civil Judge (Senior Division)/F.T.C., Lalitpur was affirmed and the revision was rejected.

sentences.text: 3. The brief facts of the case are that the marriage of the complainant was solemnized with the son of petitioner nos. 1 and 2 (the father-in-law and mother-in-law of complainant) on 07.05.2019 in accordance with Hindu rites and customs.
It is alleged that the parents of the complainant had spent substantial amounts as per their capacity and provided household articles at the time of marriage.

However, the in-laws of the complainant were not satisfied with the dowry given and allegedly subjected her to physical and mental cruelty with persistent demands for additional dowry and compelled her to leave her matrimonial home.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that petitioner nos. 1 and 2 are the father-in-law and mother-in-law, petitioner no. 3 is the devar (brother-in-law), and petitioner no. 4 is the married nanad (sister-in-law) of the complainant.

It is stated that the complainant lodged a complaint dated 06.08.2021 under Sections 147, 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, pursuant to which the learned Civil Judge (Senior Division), Lalitpur, vide order dated 20.12.2024, summoned all the petitioners to face trial under the aforesaid sections.

Aggrieved by the said summoning order, the petitioners preferred a criminal revision, which was dismissed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Lalitpur vide order dated 31.07.2025, affirming the order dated 20.12.2024 passed by the trial court.

5. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and upon perusal of the record, this Court finds that both the courts below have concurrently held that a prima facie case is made out against the petitioners.

The revisional court, upon due consideration of the material on record, has found no illegality, procedural impropriety, or jurisdictional error in the summoning order passed by the learned Magistrate.
The findings recorded by both courts are based on cogent reasoning and proper appreciation of facts, disclosing no perversity or manifest error.

6. In exercise of supervisory jurisdiction under Article 227 of the Constitution of India, this Court does not find any ground to interfere with the concurrent findings of fact recorded by the courts below, as no jurisdictional error, illegality, or perversity has been demonstrated.
The petition, being devoid of merit, is accordingly dismissed.

However, it is observed that the petitioners shall be at liberty to raise all permissible legal and factual pleas before the trial court at the appropriate stage,
which shall be considered in accordance with law.
(Vinod Diwakar,J.) November 6, 2025 A. Tripathi  Jagdish Chandel And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 6 November, 2025
